cohort: The study included 14,206 pregnancies in women with prior myomectomy and 81,517 pregnancies in women with fibroids in situ, extracted from hospital discharge data.
finding: Women with prior myomectomy had decreased rates of gestational hypertension, eclampsia, gestational diabetes, spontaneous vaginal deliveries, postpartum hemorrhage, and intrauterine fetal death, but increased risks of placenta previa, preterm delivery, cesarean section, uterine rupture, transfusions, and congenital anomalies compared to those with fibroids in situ.
mod_finding: Post-myomectomy patients experienced significantly decreased rates of spontaneous vaginal deliveries and substantially increased risks of cesarean section.
